# 12-Week Upper-Body Strength Programme: Subacromial Impingement, Recreational Climber

## Ground Rules Before You Start

- **Range:** Keep all pressing and pulling within the range she has cleared as pain-free. Unless her physio has specifically cleared it, keep arms below shoulder height on pressing and avoid loaded end-range elevation.
- **No overhead loading:** This excludes overhead press, wide-grip pull-ups, and loaded lat pulldowns to the front of the head or behind the neck.
- **Pain rule:** Pain during the exercise should stay at or below 3/10 and settle by the next morning. If it goes above that or lingers, drop the load or range, and tell her to message you before the next session.
- **Physio liaison:** Ask her physio for a written list of movements to avoid and any ROM limits, then review this plan with them at Weeks 4 and 8.
- **Sessions:** Three per week (e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri), with at least one rest day between sessions that load the shoulder.

## Phase 1: Weeks 1–4, Control and Capacity

**Goal:** Restore rotator cuff endurance, scapular control, and tolerance for loaded work. Keep loads light and reps high. Use 2 to 3 reps in reserve (RIR) on most sets.

**Session A (Mon)**
- Warm-up: Band pull-aparts, 2×15; scapular push-ups, 2×10; 3 minutes easy bike
- Side-lying external rotation (light dumbbell or towel roll), 3×12, slow 3-second lowering
- Seated cable external rotation at elbow height, 3×12
- Chest-supported row (neutral grip), 3×10–12
- Dumbbell floor press, 3×10, elbows at roughly 45°
- Pallof press, 3×10 per side
- Dead bug, 3×8 per side

**Session B (Wed)**
- Warm-up: Band face pulls at chest height, 2×15; wall slides (pain-free range only), 2×10
- Band face pull at chest height, 3×15
- Seated neutral-grip cable row, 3×10–12
- Incline dumbbell press at 30°, 3×10
- Prone or standing Y/T raises below 90° (pain-free only), 2×10 each
- Farmer carry, 3×30 seconds
- Plank on forearms, 3×20–30 seconds

**Session C (Fri)**
- Warm-up: Band pull-aparts, 2×15; band external rotation, 2×15
- Single-arm dumbbell row, 3×10 per side
- Push-ups (hands on bench or box if needed), 3×8–12, scapular control focus
- Cable chest press at chest height, 3×10
- Towel or thick-bar grip work (dead hang avoided; use towel holds on a low bar), 3×20 seconds
- Suitcase carry, 3×30 seconds per side

**Progression:** Add 1 to 2 reps per set each week when all sets are completed with good form and no pain increase. When you hit the top of the rep range across all sets, add 2.5 to 5% load.

## Phase 2: Weeks 5–8, Strength Building

**Goal:** Build loaded strength in pulling and horizontal pressing, and improve scapular stability under heavier load. Reduce reps and increase load. Use 1 to 2 RIR.

**Session A (Mon)**
- Warm-up: Band face pulls, 2×15; scapular push-ups, 2×10
- Dumbbell floor press, 4×6–8
- Chest-supported row, 4×8
- Side-lying external rotation, 3×12 (heavier band or dumbbell)
- Pallof press, 3×10 per side
- Farmer carry, 4×40 seconds

**Session B (Wed)**
- Warm-up: Band pull-aparts, 2×15; wall slides, 2×10
- Neutral-grip lat pulldown to upper chest, 4×8 (stop if any pinching or pain above 3/10; if not tolerated, substitute a row)
- Single-arm dumbbell row, 4×8 per side
- Incline dumbbell press at 30°, 3×8
- Y/T raises below 90°, 3×10
- Dead bug, 3×10 per side

**Session C (Fri)**
- Warm-up: Band external rotation, 2×15
- Push-ups, 4×10 (add load with a weight vest or feet elevated if the shoulder allows)
- Seated cable row, 4×8
- Cable external rotation at elbow height, 3×12
- Plate pinch hold, 3×20–30 seconds
- Suitcase carry, 3×40 seconds per side

**Physio review at end of Week 8.** Confirm whether ROM can be extended before Phase 3.

## Phase 3: Weeks 9–12, Climbing-Relevant Strength

# Nutrition Plan: Body Recomposition, Recreational Climber

Body recomposition means building or maintaining muscle while reducing fat. It works best with a moderate calorie deficit, high protein, and consistent training. Progress is slower than a pure cut or bulk, so set expectations accordingly and track waist measurements and strength alongside body weight.

Before you finalise anything, get her baseline data: body weight, height, age, activity level, and any medical or dietary considerations. Refer her to a GP or registered dietitian if she has a history of disordered eating, is pregnant or planning pregnancy, or takes medication that affects metabolism. The numbers below are starting points, not prescriptions.

## Step 1: Estimate Maintenance Calories

Use the Mifflin-St Jeor equation, then multiply by an activity factor.

- **Men:** (10 × weight kg) + (6.25 × height cm) − (5 × age) + 5
- **Women:** (10 × weight kg) + (6.25 × height cm) − (5 × age) − 161

For her, at age 29, the female equation applies. Multiply the result by:
- 1.4 if she trains three times a week and is otherwise fairly sedentary
- 1.55 if she is more active on non-training days (e.g., climbing outside, walking)

Example: a 65 kg, 165 cm woman would have a BMR of about 1,406 kcal. At 1.55, maintenance is about 2,180 kcal/day. Use your own figures for her.

## Step 2: Set the Calorie Target

For recomposition, aim for a modest deficit of about 10 to 15% below maintenance, or roughly 300 to 400 kcal/day. Larger deficits make it harder to hold muscle and strength during a 12-week block.

Using the example above: 2,180 minus about 300 gives a target near 1,850 to 1,900 kcal/day. Adjust after two weeks based on the trend:

- If weight is dropping faster than 0.5% of body weight per week, add 100 to 150 kcal.
- If weight is flat for two weeks and waist is unchanged, reduce by 100 kcal.
- If strength is falling across sessions, add calories before cutting further.

## Step 3: Protein

Target 1.6 to 2.2 g/kg of body weight per day. For a 65 kg client, that is roughly 105 to 140 g/day. Aim for the upper half of the range during the deficit, since it helps preserve lean mass.

Spread protein across 3 to 4 meals, with 25 to 40 g per meal. Good sources include:
- Chicken breast, turkey, lean beef, fish
- Eggs and egg whites, Greek yoghurt, cottage cheese
- Tofu, tempeh, lentils, edamame (combine varied plant sources if vegetarian or vegan)
- Whey or plant protein powder to fill gaps

## Step 4: Carbohydrates and Fats

- **Fats:** About 25 to 30% of calories, roughly 0.8 to 1 g/kg. Prioritise olive oil, nuts, seeds, oily fish, and avocado. Don't go below about 0.6 g/kg, as low fat can affect hormones and recovery.
- **Carbohydrates:** Fill the remainder. Place most carbs around training sessions to fuel work and recovery. Good options include oats, rice, potatoes, wholegrain bread, fruit, and legumes.

## Step 5: Sample Day (approx. 1,900 kcal, 120 g protein)

- **Breakfast:** Greek yoghurt (200 g) with berries, 30 g oats, and a tablespoon of chia seeds
- **Lunch:** Chicken and quinoa bowl with mixed vegetables, olive oil dressing
- **Snack:** Apple with 20 g peanut butter, or a whey shake
- **Pre-training (if training later):** Rice cakes with lean turkey and a banana
- **Dinner:** Salmon fillet (about 150 g), roasted sweet potato, green beans, a drizzle of olive oil

Adjust portions to hit her numbers. Tracking with an app for the first two weeks helps calibrate her estimates.

## Step 6: Hydration and Timing

- Aim for roughly 30 to 35 ml/kg of body weight per day from water and fluids, more on climbing or hot-training days.
- Eat a protein-and-carb meal within two to three hours before training, and include protein afterward.
- Total daily intake matters far more than precise timing for recomposition.

## Step 7: Monitoring

Each week, record:
- Average body weight (same time, same conditions, several readings)
- Waist circumference
- Session performance on the main lifts (load and reps)
- Energy, sleep quality, and appetite
- Shoulder pain response (poor nutrition can slow tendon recovery)

Review at Weeks 4, 8, and 12 alongside the physio check-ins. If body composition is the primary goal, a DEXA or skinfold assessment at baseline and Week 12 gives a more reliable picture than scale weight alone.

## Notes for Her Specifically

- Her shoulder rehab depends on adequate protein and energy, so avoid any plan that leaves her chronically under-fuelled.
- Climbing burns relatively few calories per session, so don't over-estimate training energy expenditure when adjusting intake.
- If she is planning outdoor climbing trips or hard-training weeks, bump carbohydrate intake on those days rather than cutting calories overall.

# Cardio Addition: 2 Sessions per Week

Her goal of long climbing days needs both aerobic capacity and the ability to sustain forearm and shoulder endurance over hours. Cardio should build aerobic base without adding excessive fatigue or impact to the shoulder, and it should fit around the strength sessions and her recovery.

## Principles

- **Mostly low-intensity:** Around 80% of cardio time at a conversational pace (zone 2, roughly RPE 3 to 4 out of 10). Use the remaining time for one short harder session.
- **Shoulder-friendly modes:** Prioritise cycling, walking, incline treadmill, rowing with a pain-free range (watch the catch position), and swimming only if her physio clears freestyle, since the arm recovery phase can aggravate impingement.
- **Avoid overhead and high-impact loading early:** Skip burpees, jump rope, and sprint work involving arm drive until Phase 3.
- **Schedule:** Place cardio on non-strength days or at least 6 hours apart from strength sessions. Ideal pattern with the existing Mon/Wed/Fri split: Tuesday and Saturday.

## Weekly Cardio Structure

**Session 1 (Tue): Zone 2 Base, 30 to 40 minutes**
- Stationary or outdoor bike, or incline walk
- Keep heart rate in zone 2 (roughly 60 to 70% of max HR; use the talk test if no monitor)
- Progress duration by 5 minutes every two weeks, up to 50 minutes

**Session 2 (Sat): Mixed Intensity, 25 to 35 minutes**
- 5-minute warm-up
- Intervals: 4 to 6 rounds of 2 minutes at RPE 7 (hard but controlled) with 2 minutes easy recovery
- 5-minute cool-down
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): use cycling or incline walking only
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): add rowing or ski erg if her shoulder tolerates it with no pain above 3/10
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): add longer intervals (3 to 4 minutes) and extend Session 1 to 50 minutes

## Phase Progression

| Weeks | Session 1 (Zone 2) | Session 2 (Intervals) |
|---|---|---|
| 1–4 | 30–40 min bike or incline walk | 4×2 min hard, 2 min easy |
| 5–8 | 40–45 min | 5×2 min hard, 2 min easy |
| 9–12 | 45–50 min | 4×3 min hard, 2 min easy |

## Climbing-Specific Endurance

Long climbing days depend on forearm and shoulder endurance as much as cardio. Once physio agrees, add:
- Low-load, high-rep forearm circuits (wrist curls, reverse curls, towel hangs on low bars), 2 times per week, 2 to 3 sets of 30 to 60 seconds
- Extended bouldering or traversing sessions at low intensity in Phase 3, building volume by about 10% per week

Keep total weekly volume manageable. Her shoulder is the limiting factor, so if cardio or climbing volume causes next-morning pain above 3/10, reduce the session length before reducing strength work.

## Recovery and Monitoring

- Track resting heart rate each morning. A rise of more than about 5 bpm for several days, or persistent fatigue, means reduce cardio volume for a week.
- Increase carbohydrate intake on the day before and after the longer zone 2 session and on the Saturday interval day.
- Ask her to log shoulder pain after each cardio session as well as after strength work.

## Notes for Her

- Hydrate well during longer sessions, especially if training outdoors.
- Keep Session 1 conversational. If she can't talk in full sentences, slow down.
- If she wants to climb on her cardio days, keep climbing volume low and place it after cardio, not before.

# Hangboard and Climbing-Specific Prep

## Critical Constraint: Hangboarding Loads the Shoulder Overhead

A standard hangboard session involves hanging from an edge with the arms overhead. That is overhead loading in the position she has been cleared to avoid, so **do not prescribe hangboarding until her physio explicitly clears loaded overhead elevation.** Her current clearance does not cover it, and a subacromial impingement under load at end-range elevation is the scenario this programme is designed to avoid.

Until then, grip and forearm capacity can be built in positions below shoulder height.

## Clearance Gate

Before any hanging or climbing-specific loading above the grip-only work below, confirm all of the following with her physio in writing:

- Pain-free active elevation to at least 120° (or the level the physio specifies)
- Pain-free loaded pulling with the arm below shoulder height at the planned load
- Explicit clearance for loaded overhead or hanging positions, or a stated exception for controlled dead hangs
- No night pain, and no pain above 3/10 for the 24 hours after her last strength session

If the gate is not met by Week 9, keep Phase 3 at the grip-only level and extend it. Do not force the timeline.

## Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Grip Foundation, No Hanging

**Goal:** Build forearm and finger strength in positions that keep the arm below shoulder height.

Add two sessions per week, placed on the Tuesday and Saturday cardio days or after the strength sessions with at least six hours between them:

- **Wrist curls and reverse wrist curls:** 3×15 each, moderate load, slow tempo
- **Towel pinch hold on a low bar or pinch block:** 3×20–30 seconds
- **Finger extension with a rubber band:** 3×15, to balance the pulling muscles
- **Plate pinch hold:** 3×20 seconds (progress from Phase 1 holds)
- **Half-crimp or open-hand isometric on a fingerboard at hip height:** 4×8 seconds, 3 minutes rest, only if her hands are not irritated. Keep the arm bent and the body supported, with feet on the floor.

Keep all grip work pain-free in the hands and forearms. Forearm soreness the next day is expected at low levels. Joint or tendon pain is not.

## Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Low-Height Isometrics and Conditional Hangboard

### Stage A: Grip Work Below Shoulder Height (all of Phase 3)

Continue the Phase 2 work and add:

- **Isometric pulls on a low bar or rope at hip height, body supported by feet:** 5×10 seconds, 3 times per week, as in the earlier plan. Keep elbows bent and the arm below shoulder height.
- **Towel hangs from a low bar with knees bent and feet supported:** 3×20 seconds
- **Support-hold pulls on a fingerboard with the feet on the floor:** 3×10 seconds, progressing to slightly less foot support

### Stage B: Hangboard (only if physio clears overhead loading)

Start only after written clearance. Begin with a conservative protocol and bodyweight or less:

- **Edge:** 20 mm or larger, half-crimp, with a fully straight arm hang
- **Protocol:** 7 seconds on, 3 seconds off, 6 reps per set, 3 sets, 3 minutes rest between sets
- **Load:** Start with the body weight partially supported by a chair or resistance band. Remove support gradually across sessions.
- **Frequency:** Twice per week, at least 48 hours apart, on non-strength days
- **Stop rule:** Stop any set if she feels shoulder pain above 3/10, any pinching in the shoulder, or any finger or pulley pain. Report it to her physio before the next session.

## Climbing-Specific Movement Prep

These drills keep the shoulder in a safe range while building the movement skills she needs for long days on the wall.

**Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8), 2 times per week:**
- **Traverse on a low wall or at a bouldering gym at ground level or low holds:** 15 to 20 minutes, flowing and low-intensity
- **Footwork drills:** silent feet, smearing, and heel hooks on low holds, 3×1 minute
- **Hip mobility:** 90/90 switches and hip flexor stretches, 2×60 seconds per side
- **Thoracic rotation:** open-book stretch, 2×8 per side

**Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12):**
- **Traverse volume:** Build by about 10% per week, keeping reaches below shoulder height
- **Flagging and drop-knee drills on low holds:** 3×1 minute
- **Route reading and rest-position practice:** Use lower-height problems to practise resting in a stable position
- **Bouldering at low height:** Keep problems below shoulder-height reaches. Save any overhead or dynamic moves for after physio clearance.

## Weekly Structure Update

Phases 2 and 3 now add two grip sessions and two climbing-prep sessions per week on top of the existing strength and cardio plan. Keep total weekly volume manageable. If shoulder pain or next-morning soreness rises above 3/10, cut climbing and grip volume before cutting strength work, as with the cardio guidance.

## Monitoring

- **Log after each climbing or grip session:** shoulder pain score (0–10), hand and forearm pain score, and next-morning response
- **Weekly check:** grip strength (dynamometer if available) and finger or forearm symptoms
- **Week 8 and Week 12 physio reviews:** Bring the clearance checklist and her session logs. The hangboard decision depends on this.

## Week 12 Handoff

Before she returns to full climbing:
- Confirm the physio's written clearance for overhead and hanging loads
- Record her grip strength, hang tolerance, and shoulder function score (QuickDASH or SPADI) for comparison
- Agree on a return-to-climbing progression: low-height volume first, then overhead holds, then hangboarding and long days, each step only after the previous one has been tolerated for at least two weeks

# Phase 3 Intensity Push and Peaking

Raising intensity in Phase 3 is reasonable. Peaking for a trip at Week 12 is a different question, because her climbing clearance isn't settled yet. Overhead and hanging loads are still gated, and a trip usually means overhead reaches and multi-hour days. Her shoulder needs to tolerate that before the trip, not just during the taper. So the plan below raises intensity within her cleared range, and the trip itself is conditional on physio clearance.

## Before You Start: Check the Trip Timing

Speak to her physio now, not at Week 12. Ask whether a trip involving overhead climbing is realistic by then. Two outcomes:

- **Clearance likely by Week 11:** Proceed with the peaking plan below. She can climb overhead in the final week only if the physio signs off on it.
- **Clearance unlikely:** Plan the trip for low-height bouldering or a later date. Peaking for a trip she can't fully climb risks a flare-up at the worst moment. Consider a Week 16 or 18 target instead.

Either way, the Week 12 physio review remains mandatory.

## Intensity Changes in Phase 3

Phase 3 currently uses 4×6–8 on the main pulls and presses at 1–2 RIR. Move to heavier loads with fewer reps.

**Main pulling and pressing (chest-supported row, single-arm row, floor press, incline press):**
- Weeks 9–10: 4×5–6 at 1 RIR, load up roughly 5% from Phase 2
- Week 11: 4×3–4 at 0–1 RIR, heaviest loads of the block
- Week 12: 2×3 at 2 RIR only, as a primer, not a test

**Grip and forearm work (plate pinch, towel holds, gripper):**
- Weeks 9–10: pinch holds progressed to 4×20–30 seconds with heavier plates
- Week 11: 4×15 seconds at heavier load, rest 3 minutes
- Week 12: 2×10 seconds, submaximal

**Isometric hip-height holds (5×10 seconds, 3×/week):**
- Weeks 9–10: keep as is, add load via feet-supported pulls on a lower foothold (less foot support)
- Week 11: reduce to 4 reps, increase effort to near-maximal, but keep the arm below shoulder height
- Week 12: stop

**Cardio intervals:**
- Weeks 9–10: 4×3 minutes at RPE 8, as already planned
- Week 11: 5×2 minutes at RPE 8–9 for sharpness, reduce Session 1 to 40 minutes
- Week 12: 2×1 minute at RPE 8, then easy, to keep the system primed without fatigue

**Climbing volume:** Build by about 10% per week through Week 10. In Week 11, keep low-height climbing at the same volume but add harder problems if the physio agrees. Week 12, low volume and easy movement only.

## Taper Structure

A taper shifts volume down while keeping intensity moderate, so she arrives fresh.

- **Weeks 9–10 (build):** Full volume, progressive loads. Monitor pain carefully.
- **Week 11 (peak):** Strength volume drops about 25%, intensity rises. This is the hardest week of the block.
- **Week 12 (taper):** Strength volume drops about 50%, loads stay moderate. Stop heavy grip and hip-height isometrics. Keep one short cardio session and easy climbing at low height. Schedule the Week 12 review and physio clearance before any travel.

If the trip falls after Week 12, keep the taper going into the trip week. Avoid starting a new hard session in the 48 hours before climbing.

## Stop Rules During the Push

Heavier loading raises the chance of a flare-up. Use these thresholds:

- Pain above 3/10 during a set, or pain lasting beyond 24 hours: drop the load by 10–15% for the next session, and report it to the physio.
- Any night pain, pinching, or loss of range: stop the progression for a week and contact the physio before continuing.
- Two consecutive sessions with pain above 3/10: return to Phase 2 loads for a week.

Do not progress load on any session where the previous morning's pain score was above 3/10.

## Nutrition and Recovery Adjustments

- **Weeks 9–11:** Increase carbohydrate by about 20% on the heavy strength days and on the interval day. Keep protein at the upper end of the range (around 2.0 g/kg).
- **Week 12:** Hold calories at maintenance rather than the recomposition deficit. A deficit during the taper can leave her flat on the trip. Resume the deficit after the trip if the goal still applies.
- **Sleep:** Protect 7 to 9 hours, especially in Weeks 11 and 12. Sleep quality affects tendon recovery and perceived effort more than most training variables.

## Week 12 Review

Before she travels, record:
- Pain scores across the Week 11 peak and the Week 12 taper
- Top loads and RIR on the main lifts, compared with Week 8
- Grip strength (dynamometer) and hang tolerance from grip-only work
- QuickDASH or SPADI score, compared with baseline

If the physio has not signed off on overhead and hanging loads, the trip should be low-height climbing only. Set expectations with her now so the plan doesn't push her into climbing she isn't cleared for.

# Mobility Work for Subacromial Impingement and Climbing

Mobility work for her has two jobs: restore the range that climbing and daily life need, and keep the shoulder moving without pinching. The aim is to improve thoracic extension, scapular upward rotation, posterior capsule flexibility, and hip and ankle range that support climbing posture. Mobility work supports the rehab plan, so it doesn't replace it, and anything here should follow the ROM limits her physio has set.

## Principles

- **Stay in the pain-free range.** Stretches should feel like a mild pull, never sharp or pinching. Pain above 3/10 means stop.
- **Avoid forced end-range end positions** such as aggressive overhead stretching or behind-the-back pulls until physio clears them.
- **Small, frequent doses work best.** Aim for 10 to 15 minutes, most days, rather than one long session.
- **Breathe slowly.** Relaxed breathing lowers muscle guarding and helps the shoulder move more freely.

## Daily Routine (10 to 12 minutes, 4 to 5 days per week)

Use this on non-training days and as a warm-up before strength sessions.

1. **Thoracic extension over a foam roller or bench**, 2×8 slow reps. Support the head, keep the ribs down, and extend from mid-back only.
2. **Thoracic rotation (open-book stretch)**, 2×8 per side. Lie on your side with knees bent, rotate the top arm open toward the floor while keeping the knees stacked.
3. **Cat-cow**, 2×8. Move slowly, keeping the motion through the spine rather than the lower back.
4. **Wall slides** (within cleared range), 2×10. Keep the lower back and ribs in contact with the wall. Stop before the arms rise above the point where the shoulder pinches.
5. **Sleeper stretch for posterior capsule** (only if physio approves), 2×30 seconds per side. Lie on the side with the affected arm at about 90° elbow flexion, forearm resting on the bed, and gently guide the forearm toward the floor with the other hand. Stop at a mild stretch.
6. **Cross-body shoulder stretch**, 2×30 seconds per side. Keep the shoulder down and the stretch gentle.
7. **90/90 hip switches**, 2×6 per side, for climbing hip mobility.
8. **Ankle mobility (knee-to-wall)**, 2×10 per side, for climbing footwork.

## Shoulder-Specific Mobility

These focus on the scapula and rotator cuff, which are the main contributors to impingement symptoms:

- **Scapular upward rotation with a wall walk or band**, 2×10: Gently raise the arm within pain-free range, letting the shoulder blade rotate upward and round the ribs.
- **Serratus-focused scapular push-ups**, 2×10: Start in plank on hands, let the chest drop between the shoulder blades, then push the floor away to spread them.
- **Doorway pec stretch**, 2×30 seconds per side, with the arm at or below shoulder height. Ease into it and avoid forcing the front of the shoulder.
- **Rotator cuff hold at neutral**: Hold a light band at chest height for 3×20 seconds to build control at mid-range.

## Climbing-Specific Mobility

- **Hip flexor stretch (half-kneeling)**, 2×45 seconds per side, to counter sitting and support heel hooks and high steps.
- **Hamstring and calf stretch**, 2×30 seconds per side, to support bent-leg footwork.
- **Hand and finger care**: wrist flexor and extensor stretches, 2×20 seconds each, plus gentle finger extensions after grip sessions.

## Progression by Phase

- **Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4):** Daily routine items 1–4, shoulder items with light range only.
- **Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8):** Add sleeper stretch and cross-body stretch if physio approves. Add climbing-specific hip and ankle work.
- **Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12):** Full routine. Keep stretches after strength and climbing sessions, not before heavy loads. In Week 12, reduce to the daily routine only, avoiding new end-range work in the taper.

## Stop Rules

- Sharp, pinching, or catching pain: stop the movement and reduce range.
- Pain that lingers past the next morning: reduce mobility volume for a few days and tell her physio.
- Any numbness, tingling, or night pain: stop and seek medical review.

## Notes for Her

- Mobility is not a substitute for strength. Keep the strength and grip work as the priority.
- If a stretch feels good for 30 seconds but leaves her sore the next day, she is pushing too far.
- Ask her physio to confirm the sleeper stretch and any end-range work before she adds it.

# Saturday Finisher: Full-Body Fun

This finisher follows her Saturday cardio intervals, so it needs to be full-body without adding upper-body or overhead stress. Friday is her strength day, so keep the finisher mainly lower-body and trunk-focused. Make it fun through scoring and friendly competition, not by adding load to the shoulder.

## Schedule Changes

Saturday now holds two sessions, so move the grip and climbing-prep work off Saturday:

- **Tuesday:** Zone 2 cardio, followed by grip work (at least 6 hours later if possible, or after the cardio session).
- **Thursday:** Climbing-prep and mobility work.
- **Saturday:** Interval cardio, then a 5-minute rest, then the finisher. Keep the whole session under 60 minutes.

Intensity rule: when intervals are hard, the finisher stays moderate (RPE 5–6). Keep it hard only in Phase 3 when the intervals are easier.

## Finisher Format

Use a station circuit: 40 seconds of work, 20 seconds of rest, 6 stations, 2 rounds. Track each station's rep count and score it against the previous week. A friendly leaderboard with her training partner or a group works well for motivation.

**Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Easy and Controlled**

1. Kettlebell deadlift (light, arms below chest)
2. Goblet squat to a box
3. Lateral band walks
4. Step-ups (bodyweight or light dumbbells)
5. Dead bug, 6 per side
6. Half-kneeling Pallof press

**Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Build Load and Trunk Demand**

1. Kettlebell swing (hip-driven, arms stay below chest height)
2. Goblet squat, moderate load
3. Sled push or heavy farmer carry (around the gym, 20 m)
4. Walking lunges with dumbbells held at the sides
5. Bear crawl, 15 m, only if physio has cleared quadruped weight-bearing
6. Medicine ball rotational throw against a wall, at chest height only

**Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Sharper, Still Shoulder-Safe**

1. Kettlebell swing, heavier
2. Jump squats, landing softly, arms swung low (no overhead arm drive)
3. Sled drag, backwards, to build hamstring and glute work
4. Single-leg step-ups onto a box, moderate load
5. Bear crawl or plank-to-hip-taps
6. Medicine ball Russian twists

## Week-by-Week Adjustments

- **Weeks 1–4:** 2 rounds, 40 seconds work. Focus on technique and rhythm.
- **Weeks 5–8:** Add a third round in Weeks 7–8 if the shoulder is settled. Add load to the goblet squat and carries.
- **Weeks 9–10:** Full format, higher intensity. Use a timer and try to beat last week's totals.
- **Week 11:** Peak week. Keep the finisher at 2 rounds and reduce to RPE 6–7. Skip it if her interval session was already at RPE 8–9 and she feels flat.
- **Week 12:** Taper. Keep only 1 round at easy effort, or skip the finisher entirely if she has a trip planned.

## Shoulder-Safe Rules for the Finisher

- No burpees, snatches, or any movement that drives the arms overhead.
- No jump rope until physio clears it.
- No pressing or pulling above shoulder height.
- Stop any station that causes pinching or pain above 3/10. Substitute a lower-body option instead of pushing through.
- If the next morning shows pain above 3/10 after the Saturday session, drop a round first, then a station, before changing the strength work.

## Recovery Notes

- Eat a carbohydrate-rich meal within 2 hours after the Saturday session, with at least 25 g of protein.
- Plan a full rest day or a light mobility session on Sunday.
- Ask her to log finisher scores and her shoulder response alongside her other sessions. Use the log to decide when to progress.

# 12-Week Programme: Subacromial Impingement, Recreational Climber

**Client:** 29-year-old recreational climber, right subacromial impingement, four months into physio.
**Goal:** Body recomposition, return to long climbing days, and a possible climbing trip around Week 12.
**Clearance:** Pain-free range only, no loaded overhead work until physio confirms otherwise.

## 1. Non-Negotiables

- **Pain rule:** Pain during exercise stays at or below 3/10 and settles by the next morning. Above that, or lingering, reduce load or range and message the trainer before the next session.
- **Progression rule:** Don't progress load after a session where the next-morning pain score was above 3/10.
- **Physio gates:** Written physio input at Week 0 (baseline ROM and movement exclusions), Week 4, Week 8, and Week 12. Overhead loading, hangboarding, overhead climbing, sleeper stretch, and jump rope all require explicit written clearance.
- **Trip timing:** Confirm with physio at Week 0 whether a trip involving overhead climbing is realistic by Week 11. If not, plan low-height bouldering or move the trip to Week 16 or 18.

## 2. Weekly Template

| Day | Session |
|---|---|
| Mon | Strength A + daily mobility routine |
| Tue | Zone 2 cardio (Session 1) → Grip work A (at least 6 h later, or after cardio) |
| Wed | Strength B + daily mobility routine |
| Thu | Climbing-prep (low height) + Grip work B (light) |
| Fri | Strength C + daily mobility routine |

Hangboard sessions (Weeks 9–12, Stage B only) replace Grip work A on Tuesdays if physio clears them. Keep at least 48 hours between hangboard sessions and never place them on strength days.

## 3. Strength Programme

### Phase 1: Weeks 1–4, Control and Capacity (2–3 RIR)

**Session A (Mon)**
- Band pull-aparts 2×15 and scapular push-ups 2×10 (warm-up), 3 min easy bike
- Side-lying external rotation 3×12, 3-second lowering
- Seated cable external rotation at elbow height 3×12

**Session B (Wed)**
- Band face pulls at chest height 2×15 and wall slides (pain-free) 2×10 (warm-up)
- Band face pull at chest height 3×15
- Seated neutral-grip cable row 3×10–12
- Incline dumbbell press at 30° 3×10
- Y/T raises below 90° 2×10 each
- Farmer carry 3×30 s
- Forearm plank 3×20–30 s

**Session C (Fri)**
- Band pull-aparts and band external rotation 2×15 each (warm-up)
- Single-arm dumbbell row 3×10 per side
- Push-ups (hands on bench if needed) 3×8–12
- Cable chest press at chest height 3×10
- Towel holds on a low bar 3×20 s
- Suitcase carry 3×30 s per side

**Progression:** Add 1–2 reps per set weekly when all sets are completed with good form and no pain increase. At the top of the rep range across all sets, add 2.5–5% load.

### Phase 2: Weeks 5–8, Strength Building (1–2 RIR)

**Session A (Mon)**
- Dumbbell floor press 4×6–8
- Chest-supported row 4×8
- Side-lying external rotation 3×12 (heavier)
- Pallof press 3×10 per side
- Farmer carry 4×40 s

**Session B (Wed)**
- Neutral-grip lat pulldown to upper chest 4×8 (substitute a row if any pinching or pain above 3/10)
- Single-arm dumbbell row 4×8 per side
- Incline dumbbell press at 30° 3×8
- Y/T raises below 90° 3×10
- Dead bug 3×10 per side

**Session C (Fri)**
- Push-ups 4×10 (add load with a vest or feet elevated if the shoulder allows)
- Seated cable row 4×8
- Cable external rotation at elbow height 3×12
- Plate pinch hold 3×20–30 s
- Suitcase carry 3×40 s per side

**Physio review at Week 8** before Phase 3. Confirm ROM and hangboard decision inputs.

### Phase 3: Weeks 9–12, Climbing-Relevant Strength and Peaking

**Intensity push (main lifts):**

| Week | Main pulls and presses (chest-supported row, single-arm row, floor press, incline press) |
|---|---|
| 9–10 | 4×5–6 at 1 RIR, load up about 5% from Phase 2 |
| 11 | 4×3–4 at 0–1 RIR, heaviest loads of the block (drop 1 set vs. Weeks 9–10, volume about 25% lower) |
| 12 | 2×3 at 2 RIR only, as a primer, not a test |

**Session A (Mon)**
- Chest-supported row 4×6–8 (weeks 9–10 at the push-loads above)
- Dumbbell floor press 4×6
- Neutral-grip cable row 3×10
- Side-lying external rotation 3×10 (heavier)
- Pallof press 3×10 per side
- Farmer carry 4×45 s

**Session B (Wed)**
- Single-arm dumbbell row 4×6 per side
- Neutral-grip pulldown within cleared range 4×6–8
- Incline dumbbell press 3×6–8
- Y/T raises 3×10
- Dead bug 3×10 per side

**Session C (Fri)**
- Push-ups or weighted push-ups 4×8–10
- Single-arm cable row 3×10 per side
- Plate pinch hold 4×20–30 s (weeks 9–10), 4×15 s heavier (week 11), 2×10 s submaximal (week 12)
- Gripper or thick-handle work 3×8
- Suitcase carry 3×45 s per side

**Taper rules:**
- **Week 11 (peak):** Strength volume about 25% lower, intensity higher. Hardest week of the block.
- **Week 12 (taper):** Strength volume about 50% lower, loads moderate. Stop heavy grip and hip-height isometrics after Week 11 (see Section 4).

## 4. Grip, Climbing Prep, and Hangboard

### Grip Work

**Grip work A (Tue, from Week 5):**
- Wrist curls and reverse wrist curls 3×15 each
- Towel pinch on a low bar or pinch block 3×20–30 s
- Rubber-band finger extensions 3×15
- Half-crimp or open-hand fingerboard isometric at hip height 4×8 s, 3 min rest (feet on floor, arm bent, only if hands are not irritated)

**Grip work B (Thu, from Week 5), lighter:**
- Reverse wrist curls 2×15
- Towel pinch 2×20 s
- Finger extensions 2×15

**Phase 3 additions:**
- Isometric pulls on a low bar or rope at hip height, feet supporting: 5×10 s, 3×/week (Weeks 9–10). Week 11: reduce to 4 reps at near-maximal effort. Week 12: stop.
- Towel hangs from a low bar with knees bent and feet supported: 3×20 s
- Support-hold pulls on a fingerboard with feet on the floor: 3×10 s, progressing to less foot support

Forearm soreness at low levels is expected. Joint or tendon pain is not.

### Climbing-Specific Prep (Thursday)

**Weeks 5–8:**
- Low-wall or ground-level traverse 15–20 min, flowing and low-intensity
- Footwork drills (silent feet, smearing, heel hooks on low holds) 3×1 min
- 90/90 hip switches and hip flexor stretch 2×60 s per side
- Open-book thoracic rotation 2×8 per side

**Weeks 9–10:** Traverse volume up about 10% per week, reaches below shoulder height. Add flagging and drop-knee drills 3×1 min. Practise resting positions on lower problems.

**Week 11:** Same volume, harder low-height problems if physio agrees.

**Week 12:** Low volume, easy movement, low height only.

### Hangboard (Stage B, Weeks 9–12, only after written physio clearance for overhead and hanging loads)

- Edge 20 mm or larger, half-crimp, straight-arm hang
- Protocol: 7 s on, 3 s off, 6 reps per set, 3 sets, 3 min rest
- Start with partial body-weight support (chair or band), removing support gradually
- Twice per week, 48 h apart, on Tuesdays replacing Grip work A
- **Stop** any set for shoulder pain above 3/10, pinching, or finger or pulley pain
- **Not cleared?** Stay at Stage A and extend the block. Don't force the timeline.

### Clearance Gate for Hangboard and Overhead Climbing

Confirm all of these in writing with physio:
- Pain-free active elevation to at least 120° (or the level physio sets)
- Pain-free loaded pulling below shoulder height at planned loads
- Explicit clearance for loaded overhead or hanging positions, or a stated exception for controlled dead hangs
- No night pain, and no pain above 3/10 for 24 h after the last strength session

## 5. Cardio (2 Sessions per Week)

**Session 1 (Tue): Zone 2**
- Bike or incline walk, conversational pace (RPE 3–4, about 60–70% max HR)
- Progress duration by 5 min every two weeks

**Session 2 (Sat): Intervals**
- 5 min warm-up, intervals, 5 min cool-down
- Phase 1: cycling or incline walking only
- Phase 2: rowing or ski erg added if pain stays at or below 3/10

| Weeks | Session 1 (Zone 2) | Session 2 (Intervals) |
|---|---|---|
| 1–4 | 30–40 min | 4×2 min at RPE 7, 2 min easy |
| 5–8 | 40–45 min | 5×2 min at RPE 7, 2 min easy |
| 9–10 | 45–50 min | 4×3 min at RPE 8, 2 min easy |
| 11 | 40 min | 5×2 min at RPE 8–9, 2 min easy |
| 12 | 30 min easy | 2×1 min at RPE 8, then easy |

Swimming freestyle only with physio clearance (arm recovery can aggravate impingement). Skip burpees, jump rope, and arm-driven sprints until cleared.

## 6. Saturday Finisher

Format: station circuit, 40 s work, 20 s rest, 6 stations, 2 rounds (weeks 7–8: add a third round if the shoulder is settled). Log reps per station and beat last week's total. Keep RPE at 5–6 on days when intervals are hard.

**Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4):**
1. Light kettlebell deadlift (arms below chest)
2. Goblet squat to a box
3. Lateral band walks
4. Step-ups (bodyweight or light dumbbells)
5. Dead bug, 6 per side
6. Half-kneeling Pallof press

**Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8):**
1. Hip-driven kettlebell swing (arms below chest)
2. Goblet squat, moderate load
3. Sled push or heavy farmer carry, 20 m
4. Dumbbell walking lunges (arms at sides)
5. Bear crawl 15 m (only if physio clears quadruped weight-bearing)
6. Medicine ball rotational throw against a wall at chest height

**Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12):**
1. Heavier kettlebell swing
2. Jump squats, soft landing, arms swung low (no overhead drive)
3. Backward sled drag
4. Single-leg box step-ups, moderate load
5. Bear crawl or plank-to-hip-taps
6. Medicine ball Russian twists

**Weekly finisher adjustments:**
- Week 11: 2 rounds at RPE 6–7. Skip if intervals were RPE 8–9 and she feels flat.
- Week 12: 1 easy round, or skip if travelling.

**Finisher rules:** No overhead arm drive, no pressing or pulling above shoulder height. Substitute a lower-body station for any station causing pinching or pain above 3/10. If next-morning pain is above 3/10, drop a round first, then a station, before touching strength work.

## 7. Mobility Routine

**Daily routine (10–12 min, 4–5 days a week, also as warm-up before strength):**
1. Thoracic extension over a foam roller 2×8
2. Open-book thoracic rotation 2×8 per side
3. Cat-cow 2×8
4. Wall slides (pain-free range) 2×10
5. Cross-body shoulder stretch 2×30 s per side
6. 90/90 hip switches 2×6 per side
7. Knee-to-wall ankle mobility 2×10 per side

**Shoulder-specific (add as tolerated):**
- Scapular upward rotation on a wall walk 2×10
- Serratus scapular push-ups 2×10
- Doorway pec stretch at or below shoulder height 2×30 s per side
- Band hold at chest height (neutral) 3×20 s

**Gated (physio approval needed):** Sleeper stretch for the posterior capsule, 2×30 s per side. Add in Phase 2 only if cleared.

**Climbing-specific:** Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch 2×45 s per side; hamstring and calf stretch 2×30 s per side; wrist flexor and extensor stretches 2×20 s each, plus finger extensions after grip work.

**Phase notes:** Phase 1 uses routine items 1–4 and light-range shoulder work only. Phase 2 adds the cross-body stretch and climbing-specific hip and ankle work. Phase 3 is the full routine, performed after strength and climbing sessions. In Week 12, reduce to the daily routine only.

**Stop rules:** Sharp, pinching, or catching pain means stop and reduce range. Pain lingering to the next morning means reduce volume for a few days and tell physio. Any numbness, tingling, or night pain means stop and seek medical review.

## 8. Nutrition: Body Recomposition

**Baseline:** Record weight, height, age, activity level, medical history, and dietary needs. Refer to a GP or registered dietitian if there is any history of disordered eating, pregnancy or plans to conceive, or medication affecting metabolism.

**Calories:**
- Estimate maintenance with Mifflin-St Jeor (female equation), then multiply by 1.4 (three sessions per week, otherwise sedentary) or 1.55 (more active on non-training days).
- Set the target 10–15% below maintenance (about 300–400 kcal deficit).
- Review after two weeks:
  - Losing faster than 0.5% of body weight per week: add 100–150 kcal.
  - Flat weight and waist for two weeks: reduce by 100 kcal.
  - Strength falling across sessions: add calories before cutting further.

**Protein:** 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day, aiming for the upper half (around 2.0 g/kg) during the deficit. Spread across 3–4 meals with 25–40 g each.

**Fats:** 25–30% of calories, about 0.8–1 g/kg, not below 0.6 g/kg.

**Carbohydrates:** Fill the remainder, concentrated around training. Increase by about 20% on heavy strength days (Weeks 9–11) and on interval days. Increase on the day before and after the long zone 2 session.

**Hydration:** About 30–35 ml/kg/day, more on climbing or hot days.

**Phase adjustments:**
- Weeks 1–8: standard deficit.
- Weeks 9–11: protein at the upper end, carbohydrates raised as above.
- Week 12: hold calories at maintenance for the taper and trip. Resume the deficit afterward if the goal still applies.

**Sleep:** 7–9 hours, especially in Weeks 11–12.

**Sample day (about 1,900 kcal, 120 g protein at a 65 kg example):** Greek yoghurt with berries, oats and chia; chicken and quinoa bowl with vegetables and olive oil; apple with peanut butter or a whey shake; rice cakes with turkey and banana before training; salmon, sweet potato, green beans for dinner. Adjust to her numbers.

## 9. Monitoring

**Each session:** Log shoulder pain (0–10) during and next morning, hand and forearm pain for grip or climbing sessions, and loads and reps.

**Each week:** Average body weight (several readings, same conditions), waist circumference, grip strength (dynamometer if available), energy, sleep, and appetite.

**Physio gates:** Weeks 0, 4, 8, and 12. Bring the clearance checklist and session logs.

**Baseline and Week 12:** DEXA or skinfold assessment, plus QuickDASH or SPADI.

## 10. Week-by-Week Summary

| Week | Strength | Grip and climbing prep | Cardio | Finisher | Nutrition |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1–4 | Phase 1, 2–3 RIR | Mobility only | Zone 2 30–40 min; intervals 4×2 | Phase 1, 2 rounds | Deficit, protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg |
| 4 | Physio review | Review hand and forearm symptoms | Continue | Continue | Review trend, adjust calories |
| 5–8 | Phase 2, 1–2 RIR | Grip A and B; low traverses; hip and footwork work | Zone 2 40–45; intervals 5×2 | Phase 2; add round 3 in Weeks 7–8 if settled | Continue; review at Week 8 |
| 8 | Physio review, hangboard decision inputs | Review | Continue | Continue | Review |
| 9–10 | Phase 3 push: 4×5–6 at 1 RIR, +5% load | Isometrics 5×10 s, 3×/week; hangboard only if cleared; traverse volume +10%/week | Zone 2 45–50; intervals 4×3 at RPE 8 | Phase 3, higher intensity, beat last week | Protein upper end; carbs +20% on heavy days |
| 11 | Peak: 4×3–4 at 0–1 RIR, volume −25% | Isometrics reduced to 4 near-max reps; harder low-height problems if cleared | 40 min Zone 2; 5×2 at RPE 8–9 | 2 rounds at RPE 6–7 (skip if flat) | Protein upper end, carbs up, sleep priority |
| 12 | Primer: 2×3 at 2 RIR; volume −50% | Stop isometrics; easy low-height climbing only | 30 min easy; 2×1 min at RPE 8 | 1 easy round or skip | Hold maintenance calories |

## 11. Stop Rules and Escalation

- **Pain above 3/10 during a set, or lasting beyond 24 hours:** Drop load 10–15% next session and report to physio.
- **Night pain, pinching, or loss of range:** Stop progression for a week and contact physio.
- **Two consecutive sessions above 3/10:** Return to Phase 2 loads for one week.
- **Numbness, tingling, or persistent night pain:** Stop and seek medical review.

Reduction order when pain rises: climbing and grip volume first, then finisher and cardio, then strength load. Protect strength work where possible, as it's the main shoulder-protective intervention.

## 12. Week 12 Review and Trip Handoff

Before any travel, record and review:
- Pain scores across the Week 11 peak and Week 12 taper
- Top loads and RIR on main lifts compared with Week 8
- Grip strength and hang tolerance from grip-only work
- QuickDASH or SPADI compared with baseline
- Written physio sign-off for overhead and hanging loads

**If physio has not signed off:** the trip is low-height climbing only. Set this expectation with her in Week 9 so the plan doesn't push her into climbing she isn't cleared for.

**Return-to-climbing progression (after Week 12):** Low-height volume first, then overhead holds, then hangboarding and long days. Move to each step only after two weeks of tolerance at the previous one.

# 12-Week Programme: Subacromial Impingement, Recreational Climber

**Client:** 29-year-old recreational climber, right subacromial impingement, four months into physio.
**Goal:** Body recomposition, return to long climbing days, and a possible climbing trip around Week 12.
**Clearance:** Pain-free range only, no loaded overhead work until physio confirms otherwise.

## 1. Non-Negotiables

- **Pain rule:** Pain during exercise stays at or below 3/10 and settles by the next morning. Above that, or lingering, reduce load or range and message the trainer before the next session.
- **Progression rule:** Don't progress load after a session where the next-morning pain score was above 3/10.
- **Physio gates:** Written physio input at Week 0 (baseline ROM and movement exclusions), Week 4, Week 8, and Week 12. Overhead loading, hangboarding, overhead climbing, sleeper stretch, and jump rope all require explicit written clearance.
- **Trip timing:** Confirm with physio at Week 0 whether a trip involving overhead climbing is realistic by Week 11. If not, plan low-height bouldering or move the trip to Week 16 or 18.

## 2. Weekly Template

| Day | Session |
|---|---|
| Mon | Strength A + daily mobility routine |
| Tue | Zone 2 cardio (Session 1) → Grip work A (at least 6 h later, or after cardio) |
| Wed | Strength B + daily mobility routine |
| Thu | Climbing-prep (low height) + Grip work B (light) |
| Fri | Strength C + daily mobility routine |
| Sat | Interval cardio (Session 2) → 5 min rest → Saturday finisher (total under 60 min) |
| Sun | Full rest or light mobility only |

Hangboard sessions (Weeks 9–12, Stage B only) replace Grip work A on Tuesdays if physio clears them. Keep at least 48 hours between hangboard sessions and never place them on strength days.

## 3. Strength Programme

### Phase 1: Weeks 1–4, Control and Capacity (2–3 RIR)

**Session A (Mon)**
- Band pull-aparts 2×15 and scapular push-ups 2×10 (warm-up), 3 min easy bike
- Side-lying external rotation 3×12, 3-second lowering
- Seated cable external rotation at elbow height 3×12
- Chest-supported row, neutral grip, 3×10–12
- Dumbbell floor press, elbows at about 45°, 3×10
- Pallof press 3×10 per side
- Dead bug 3×8 per side

**Session B (Wed)**
- Band face pulls at chest height 2×15 and wall slides (pain-free) 2×10 (warm-up)
- Band face pull at chest height 3×15
- Seated neutral-grip cable row 3×10–12
- Incline dumbbell press at 30° 3×10
- Y/T raises below 90° 2×10 each
- Farmer carry 3×30 s
- Forearm plank 3×20–30 s

**Session C (Fri)**
- Band pull-aparts and band external rotation 2×15 each (warm-up)
- Single-arm dumbbell row 3×10 per side
- Push-ups (hands on bench if needed) 3×8–12
- Cable chest press at chest height 3×10
- Towel holds on a low bar 3×20 s
- Suitcase carry 3×30 s per side

**Progression:** Add 1–2 reps per set weekly when all sets are completed with good form and no pain increase. At the top of the rep range across all sets, add 2.5–5% load.

### Phase 2: Weeks 5–8, Strength Building (1–2 RIR)

**Session A (Mon)**
- Dumbbell floor press 4×6–8
- Chest-supported row 4×8
- Side-lying external rotation 3×12 (heavier)
- Pallof press 3×10 per side
- Farmer carry 4×40 s

**Session B (Wed)**
- Neutral-grip lat pulldown to upper chest 4×8 (substitute a row if any pinching or pain above 3/10)
- Single-arm dumbbell row 4×8 per side
- Incline dumbbell press at 30° 3×8
- Y/T raises below 90° 3×10
- Dead bug 3×10 per side

**Session C (Fri)**
- Push-ups 4×10 (add load with a vest or feet elevated if the shoulder allows)
- Seated cable row 4×8
- Cable external rotation at elbow height 3×12
- Plate pinch hold 3×20–30 s
- Suitcase carry 3×40 s per side

**Physio review at Week 8** before Phase 3. Confirm ROM and hangboard decision inputs.

### Phase 3: Weeks 9–12, Climbing-Relevant Strength and Peaking

**Intensity push (main lifts):**

| Week | Main pulls and presses (chest-supported row, single-arm row, floor press, incline press) |
|---|---|
| 9–10 | 4×5–6 at 1 RIR, load up about 5% from Phase 2 |
| 11 | 4×3–4 at 0–1 RIR, heaviest loads of the block (drop 1 set vs. Weeks 9–10, volume about 25% lower) |
| 12 | 2×3 at 2 RIR only, as a primer, not a test |

**Session A (Mon)**
- Chest-supported row 4×6–8 (weeks 9–10 at the push-loads above)
- Dumbbell floor press 4×6
- Neutral-grip cable row 3×10
- Side-lying external rotation 3×10 (heavier)
- Pallof press 3×10 per side
- Farmer carry 4×45 s

**Session B (Wed)**
- Single-arm dumbbell row 4×6 per side
- Neutral-grip pulldown within cleared range 4×6–8
- Incline dumbbell press 3×6–8
- Y/T raises 3×10
- Dead bug 3×10 per side

**Session C (Fri)**
- Push-ups or weighted push-ups 4×8–10
- Single-arm cable row 3×10 per side
- Plate pinch hold 4×20–30 s (weeks 9–10), 4×15 s heavier (week 11), 2×10 s submaximal (week 12)
- Gripper or thick-handle work 3×8
- Suitcase carry 3×45 s per side

**Taper rules:**
- **Week 11 (peak):** Strength volume about 25% lower, intensity higher. Hardest week of the block.
- **Week 12 (taper):** Strength volume about 50% lower, loads moderate. Stop heavy grip and hip-height isometrics after Week 11 (see Section 4).

## 4. Grip, Climbing Prep, and Hangboard

### Grip Work

**Grip work A (Tue, from Week 5):**
- Wrist curls and reverse wrist curls 3×15 each
- Towel pinch on a low bar or pinch block 3×20–30 s
- Rubber-band finger extensions 3×15
- Half-crimp or open-hand fingerboard isometric at hip height 4×8 s, 3 min rest (feet on floor, arm bent, only if hands are not irritated)

**Grip work B (Thu, from Week 5), lighter:**
- Reverse wrist curls 2×15
- Towel pinch 2×20 s
- Finger extensions 2×15

**Phase 3 additions:**
- Isometric pulls on a low bar or rope at hip height, feet supporting: 5×10 s, 3×/week (Weeks 9–10). Week 11: reduce to 4 reps at near-maximal effort. Week 12: stop.
- Towel hangs from a low bar with knees bent and feet supported: 3×20 s
- Support-hold pulls on a fingerboard with feet on the floor: 3×10 s, progressing to less foot support

Forearm soreness at low levels is expected. Joint or tendon pain is not.

### Climbing-Specific Prep (Thursday)

**Weeks 5–8:**
- Low-wall or ground-level traverse 15–20 min, flowing and low-intensity
- Footwork drills (silent feet, smearing, heel hooks on low holds) 3×1 min
- 90/90 hip switches and hip flexor stretch 2×60 s per side
- Open-book thoracic rotation 2×8 per side

**Weeks 9–10:** Traverse volume up about 10% per week, reaches below shoulder height. Add flagging and drop-knee drills 3×1 min. Practise resting positions on lower problems.

**Week 11:** Same volume, harder low-height problems if physio agrees.

**Week 12:** Low volume, easy movement, low height only.

### Hangboard (Stage B, Weeks 9–12, only after written physio clearance for overhead and hanging loads)

- Edge 20 mm or larger, half-crimp, straight-arm hang
- Protocol: 7 s on, 3 s off, 6 reps per set, 3 sets, 3 min rest
- Start with partial body-weight support (chair or band), removing support gradually
- Twice per week, 48 h apart, on Tuesdays replacing Grip work A
- **Stop** any set for shoulder pain above 3/10, pinching, or finger or pulley pain
- **Not cleared?** Stay at Stage A and extend the block. Don't force the timeline.

### Clearance Gate for Hangboard and Overhead Climbing

Confirm all of these in writing with physio:
- Pain-free active elevation to at least 120° (or the level physio sets)
- Pain-free loaded pulling below shoulder height at planned loads
- Explicit clearance for loaded overhead or hanging positions, or a stated exception for controlled dead hangs
- No night pain, and no pain above 3/10 for 24 h after the last strength session

## 5. Cardio (2 Sessions per Week)

**Session 1 (Tue): Zone 2**
- Bike or incline walk, conversational pace (RPE 3–4, about 60–70% max HR)
- Progress duration by 5 min every two weeks

**Session 2 (Sat): Intervals**
- 5 min warm-up, intervals, 5 min cool-down
- Phase 1: cycling or incline walking only
- Phase 2: rowing or ski erg added if pain stays at or below 3/10

| Weeks | Session 1 (Zone 2) | Session 2 (Intervals) |
|---|---|---|
| 1–4 | 30–40 min | 4×2 min at RPE 7, 2 min easy |
| 5–8 | 40–45 min | 5×2 min at RPE 7, 2 min easy |
| 9–10 | 45–50 min | 4×3 min at RPE 8, 2 min easy |
| 11 | 40 min | 5×2 min at RPE 8–9, 2 min easy |
| 12 | 30 min easy | 2×1 min at RPE 8, then easy |

Swimming freestyle only with physio clearance (arm recovery can aggravate impingement). Skip burpees, jump rope, and arm-driven sprints until cleared.

## 6. Saturday Finisher

Format: station circuit, 40 s work, 20 s rest, 6 stations, 2 rounds (weeks 7–8: add a third round if the shoulder is settled). Log reps per station and beat last week's total. Keep RPE at 5–6 on days when intervals are hard.

**Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4):**
1. Light kettlebell deadlift (arms below chest)
2. Goblet squat to a box
3. Lateral band walks
4. Step-ups (bodyweight or light dumbbells)
5. Dead bug, 6 per side
6. Half-kneeling Pallof press

**Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8):**
1. Hip-driven kettlebell swing (arms below chest)
2. Goblet squat, moderate load
3. Sled push or heavy farmer carry, 20 m
4. Dumbbell walking lunges (arms at sides)
5. Bear crawl 15 m (only if physio clears quadruped weight-bearing)
6. Medicine ball rotational throw against a wall at chest height

**Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12):**
1. Heavier kettlebell swing
2. Jump squats, soft landing, arms swung low (no overhead drive)
3. Backward sled drag
4. Single-leg box step-ups, moderate load
5. Bear crawl or plank-to-hip-taps
6. Medicine ball Russian twists

**Weekly finisher adjustments:**
- Week 11: 2 rounds at RPE 6–7. Skip if intervals were RPE 8–9 and she feels flat.
- Week 12: 1 easy round, or skip if travelling.

**Finisher rules:** No overhead arm drive, no pressing or pulling above shoulder height. Substitute a lower-body station for any station causing pinching or pain above 3/10. If next-morning pain is above 3/10, drop a round first, then a station, before touching strength work.

## 7. Mobility Routine

**Daily routine (10–12 min, 4–5 days a week, also as warm-up before strength):**
1. Thoracic extension over a foam roller 2×8
2. Open-book thoracic rotation 2×8 per side
3. Cat-cow 2×8
4. Wall slides (pain-free range) 2×10
5. Cross-body shoulder stretch 2×30 s per side
6. 90/90 hip switches 2×6 per side
7. Knee-to-wall ankle mobility 2×10 per side

**Shoulder-specific (add as tolerated):**
- Scapular upward rotation on a wall walk 2×10
- Serratus scapular push-ups 2×10
- Doorway pec stretch at or below shoulder height 2×30 s per side
- Band hold at chest height (neutral) 3×20 s

**Gated (physio approval needed):** Sleeper stretch for the posterior capsule, 2×30 s per side. Add in Phase 2 only if cleared.

**Climbing-specific:** Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch 2×45 s per side; hamstring and calf stretch 2×30 s per side; wrist flexor and extensor stretches 2×20 s each, plus finger extensions after grip work.

**Phase notes:** Phase 1 uses routine items 1–4 and light-range shoulder work only. Phase 2 adds the cross-body stretch and climbing-specific hip and ankle work. Phase 3 is the full routine, performed after strength and climbing sessions. In Week 12, reduce to the daily routine only.

**Stop rules:** Sharp, pinching, or catching pain means stop and reduce range. Pain lingering to the next morning means reduce volume for a few days and tell physio. Any numbness, tingling, or night pain means stop and seek medical review.

## 8. Nutrition: Body Recomposition

**Baseline:** Record weight, height, age, activity level, medical history, and dietary needs. Refer to a GP or registered dietitian if there is any history of disordered eating, pregnancy or plans to conceive, or medication affecting metabolism.

**Calories:**
- Estimate maintenance with Mifflin-St Jeor (female equation), then multiply by 1.4 (three sessions per week, otherwise sedentary) or 1.55 (more active on non-training days).
- Set the target 10–15% below maintenance (about 300–400 kcal deficit).
- Review after two weeks:
  - Losing faster than 0.5% of body weight per week: add 100–150 kcal.
  - Flat weight and waist for two weeks: reduce by 100 kcal.
  - Strength falling across sessions: add calories before cutting further.

**Protein:** 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day, aiming for the upper half (around 2.0 g/kg) during the deficit. Spread across 3–4 meals with 25–40 g each.

**Fats:** 25–30% of calories, about 0.8–1 g/kg, not below 0.6 g/kg.

**Carbohydrates:** Fill the remainder, concentrated around training. Increase by about 20% on heavy strength days (Weeks 9–11) and on interval days. Increase on the day before and after the long zone 2 session.

**Hydration:** About 30–35 ml/kg/day, more on climbing or hot days.

**Phase adjustments:**
- Weeks 1–8: standard deficit.
- Weeks 9–11: protein at the upper end, carbohydrates raised as above.
- Week 12: hold calories at maintenance for the taper and trip. Resume the deficit afterward if the goal still applies.

**Sleep:** 7–9 hours, especially in Weeks 11–12.

**Sample day (about 1,900 kcal, 120 g protein at a 65 kg example):** Greek yoghurt with berries, oats and chia; chicken and quinoa bowl with vegetables and olive oil; apple with peanut butter or a whey shake; rice cakes with turkey and banana before training; salmon, sweet potato, green beans for dinner. Adjust to her numbers.

## 9. Monitoring

**Each session:** Log shoulder pain (0–10) during and next morning, hand and forearm pain for grip or climbing sessions, and loads and reps.

**Each week:** Average body weight (several readings, same conditions), waist circumference, grip strength (dynamometer if available), energy, sleep, and appetite.

**Physio gates:** Weeks 0, 4, 8, and 12. Bring the clearance checklist and session logs.

**Baseline and Week 12:** DEXA or skinfold assessment, plus QuickDASH or SPADI.

## 10. Week-by-Week Summary

| Week | Strength | Grip and climbing prep | Cardio | Finisher | Nutrition |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1–4 | Phase 1, 2–3 RIR | Mobility only | Zone 2 30–40 min; intervals 4×2 | Phase 1, 2 rounds | Deficit, protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg |
| 4 | Physio review | Review hand and forearm symptoms | Continue | Continue | Review trend, adjust calories |

## 11. Stop Rules and Escalation

- **Pain above 3/10 during a set, or lasting beyond 24 hours:** Drop load 10–15% next session and report to physio.
- **Night pain, pinching, or loss of range:** Stop progression for a week and contact physio.
- **Two consecutive sessions above 3/10:** Return to Phase 2 loads for one week.
- **Numbness, tingling, or persistent night pain:** Stop and seek medical review.

Reduction order when pain rises: climbing and grip volume first, then finisher and cardio, then strength load. Protect strength work where possible, as it's the main shoulder-protective intervention.

## 12. Week 12 Review and Trip Handoff

Before any travel, record and review:
- Pain scores across the Week 11 peak and Week 12 taper
- Top loads and RIR on main lifts compared with Week 8
- Grip strength and hang tolerance from grip-only work
- QuickDASH or SPADI compared with baseline
- Written physio sign-off for overhead and hanging loads

**If physio has not signed off:** the trip is low-height climbing only. Set this expectation with her in Week 9 so the plan doesn't push her into climbing she isn't cleared for.

**Return-to-climbing progression (after Week 12):** Low-height volume first, then overhead holds, then hangboarding and long days. Move to each step only after two weeks of tolerance at the previous one.
